system:
You extract quantitative facts about one clinical trial programme from one document.

Rules:
- Extract only facts stated in THIS document. Never use outside knowledge.
- Every fact needs "quote": an exact, verbatim span copied from the document (8-300 characters) that contains the number. Quotes are machine-checked; paraphrases are discarded.
- Placebo-adjusted values are preferred. If a value is within-arm (not placebo-adjusted), set attrs.placebo_adjusted=false.
- Units: keep the unit the document uses; put it in "unit".
- Other trials of the same investigational drug (phase 2, dose-finding, other populations, combination arms) belong
  to the programme: extract their facts too, and put the trial's name in attrs.trial when the document gives it.
- Return {"facts": []} only if the document reports no results for the investigational drug.

Allowed keys:
  n_randomized, median_followup, primary_endpoint, inclusion_threshold, planned_events, assumed_rrr, power,
  alpha, stopped_early, events_treatment, events_control, events_total, hr, ci_low, ci_high, p_value,
  biomarker_change, baseline_level, sbp_change, safety_signal, readout_statement

For biomarker_change and baseline_level, attrs must include: biomarker (one of LDL-C, non-HDL-C, apoB, HDL-C,
Lp(a), triglycerides, hsCRP, IL-6, Lp-PLA2 activity, sPLA2-IIA, SBP, other), phase (phase2 or phase3),
timepoint, method (assay or "not stated"), placebo_adjusted (true/false), dose (if stated).
For biomarker_change give "value" as the change (negative = reduction) and state in attrs.kind whether it is
"percent" or "absolute".

Return JSON only:
{"facts": [{"key": "...", "value": <number or string>, "unit": "...", "attrs": {...}, "quote": "..."}]}
prompt:
Trial: VISTA-16 NCT01130246 - VISTA-16 Trial: Evaluation of Safety and Efficacy of Short-term A-002 Treatment in Subjects With Acute Coronary Syndrome
Investigational drug: varespladib
Document: Anti-inflammatory effects of varespladib methyl in diabetic patients with acute coronary syndrome. (journal, published 2011-12-01, source pmid:21989792)

--- DOCUMENT TEXT ---
Anti-inflammatory effects of varespladib methyl in diabetic patients with acute coronary syndrome.

Purpose Secretory phospholipase A(2) group IIA (sPLA(2-)IIA) concentration and activity are associated with increased risk of cardiovascular events in acute coronary syndrome (ACS) patients. This study evaluated baseline differences in sPLA(2)-IIA concentration and other inflammatory markers in ACS patients with and without diabetes, and the inflammatory biomarker response to selective sPLA(2) inhibition. Methods The effects of the sPLA(2) inhibitor varespladib methyl 500 mg daily and placebo on serial changes in inflammatory and lipid biomarkers were examined in 624 ACS patients who were treated with standard of care including atorvastatin 80 mg daily. Results Compared with non-diabetic patients, diabetic patients had higher baseline concentrations of sPLA(2)-IIA (p = 0.0066), hs-CRP (p = 0.0155), and IL-6 (p = 0.009). At 8 weeks of treatment (primary endpoint), varespladib methyl reduced median sPLA(2)-IIA levels by -83.6% in diabetic patients and by -82.4% in non-diabetic patients (p = 0.33). Median hs-CRP and IL-6 levels were reduced in both varespladib methyl-treated diabetic and non-diabetic patients, but these differences were not statistically significantly different at 8 weeks (p = 0.57 and p = 0.97 respectively). Conclusions Varespladib significantly reduces the post-ACS inflammatory response in those with and without diabetes. These responses were greater in diabetic subjects compared to non-diabetic subjects.
--- END ---
